passage: I'm Pooja, and I sit behind Irfan in assembly. Irfan doesn't say the prayer and doesn't make trouble, just stands with hands folded. At lunch, only to me, Irfan said, "There's no god for me, and it feels lonely. Everyone just assumes." I said nothing clever. I moved my tiffin closer. Later in the library Irfan showed me a book on stars and said, "When I read this I feel small in a good way." I also saw Irfan help the caretaker carry chairs without being asked. I can't say the loneliness is gone, but Irfan asked if I'd come to the astronomy club on Friday.

qa.q: What did Irfan show Pooja in the library?
qa.a: Irfan showed Pooja a book on stars.

qa.q: What does Irfan feel about not believing, and how does Pooja know?
qa.a: Irfan feels lonely, because Irfan said so at lunch, and also a sense of awe when reading about the stars.

qa.q: What could Irfan do to feel less alone?
qa.a: Find people, books and values to rely on, such as the astronomy club, and keep the kindness that already shows in helping.

qa.q: How might Pooja's moving the tiffin closer matter to Irfan?
qa.a: It may have shown company without judgement, though Pooja cannot be sure how it felt to Irfan.

grounding: Irfan feels lonely in not believing in any god, and an observer sees awe, ethics and a first move toward people who share Irfan's interests.
